CLIMATE ACTION 
 
Draft Kilkenny County Council Climate Action 
Plan   
The Draft Kilkenny County Council Climate 
Action Plan is out for public consultation until 20th 
December. It is a statutory 5-year Plan which 
outlines the measures that Kilkenny County 
Council will take to reduce energy use and carbon 
emissions, and adapt to the changing climate 
across its governance, services and operations. In 
addition, it sets out how Kilkenny County Council 
will facilitate, support and inspire stakeholder 
climate action in the County through leadership, 
collaboration and advocacy. 
 
This Plan has been prepared in close collaboration 
with the Kilkenny County Council Climate Action 
Steering Committee, relevant staff from every 
service area in the local authority and Elected 
Representatives. Input has been provided by 
Strategic Policy Committee 4 (Environmental 
Protection, Climate and Energy), the Public 
Participation Network (PPN), the Climate Action 
Regional Office, adjoining local authorities, 
business and community stakeholders and the 
public. 
 
The Plan is informed by the most recent scientific 
data and evidence. Six specialist reports were 
commissioned as part of the preparation of the 
Plan and the findings of these have been 
assimilated into the Plan. The key climate risks 
facing 
County 
Kilkenny, 
along 
with 
the 
greenhouse gas emissions produced by Kilkenny 
County Council and the County are presented. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
96 actions were developed, and these will be 
undertaken by Kilkenny County Council over the 
next five years. By delivering these actions 
Kilkenny County Council will reduce its own 
greenhouse gas emissions by 51% and improve its 
energy efficiency by 50%.

5 
 
It will also implement measures to prepare for climate change, support resilience and provide other benefits 
such as improved health and well-being, enhanced biodiversity, green job creation, sustainable use of 
materials and the circular economy. Collaboration with stakeholders including business, the community 
and other public sector organisations will be vital to the success of the Plan. 
 
As part of the preparation of the Plan, Local Authorities are required to identify a Decarbonising Zone (DZ) 
– an area within the County which will act as a test bed for trialling what is possible for decarbonisation 
and climate action at a local and community level.  Kilkenny City has been identified as the DZ for County 
Kilkenny. Building on its socioeconomic and environmental characteristics, the Kilkenny City DZ has a 
strong foundation of existing assets and services, with the potential to deliver a wide-range of 
decarbonisation opportunities

Reduce your Use Energy Campaign 
The Kilkenny County Council “Reduce Your Use” energy campaign for Winter ‘2023/24 is underway. 
Running from October 2023 to March 2024, the campaign consists of a programme of themed activities to 
promote energy efficiency within the organisation.   
 
As part of the campaign, we have communicated with all staff to 
take simple measures to reduce energy use over the winter 
months. The Council has also selected the Thomastown and 
Callan Area Offices as a pilot area and is preparing Energy 
Reduction Plans to identify key works and changes in behaviour 
required to help reduce energy use in the Area Offices. 
 
The campaign will be documented over the next few months, and 
a short video will be produced to communicate the key findings 
and results from the campaign. More details on the Reduce Your 
Use Campaign can be seen on the Climate Action page of the 
Kilkenny County Council Website. 
https://www.kilkennycoco.ie/eng/services/environment/climate-
action/reduce-your-use.html 
 
Electrical Vehicle (EV) Demo at County Hall 
Thanks to the Machinery Yard for organising an EV demo at County Hall from 22nd–24th November where 
Lyng Motors kindly brought EV’s for staff to test drive and to find out more about the technology and learn 
what it is like to own an EV. Data commissioned by the Climate Action Office shows that transport is 
responsible for 36% of the green-house gas produced in Kilkenny City, so supporting people to walk, cycle, 
take public transport and move away from fossil fuels is vital in tacking the climate crisis at a local level. 
 
Funding to help communities take Climate Action  
The Community Climate Action Fund is expected to open to applications on the 6th December 2023. It is 
envisaged to be very well received by communities with plenty of interest to date. Our Community Climate 
Action Officer (CCAO), Breda Maher, has met over 30 communities to date to support and encourage them 
to look at any potential projects that would have a direct climate action impact and benefit their community.

6 
 
Successful applicants under this scheme will deliver a variety of projects which support them and help to 
build low carbon communities. Kilkenny County Council has received an allocation of €511,000 grant 
funding from the Department of Environment, Climate and Communications for the fund and there is 100% 
funding for successful applicants. 
 
Upon launch of this programme, the Climate Action Office will issue a press release and communicate 
through all our channels and networks. A webinar will also be held in January to answer questions and

Waste Enforcement 
Kilkenny County Council had 57 enforcement files opened so far in 2023. Three cases have been before the 
District Court, with another case in the High Court for recovery of the landfill levy.  
 
Our use of CCTV will be approved shortly following agreement of draft guidance with the Data 
Commissioner. The draft guidance will see risk assessments for all uses of mobile recording devices and 
greater emphasis placed on the need to have such systems in operation and ensuring GDPR compliance.  
 
In October we finalised training for our drone within the Waste Enforcement Section. We have a 3D 
mapping drone that we will use to inspect and investigate authorised and unauthorised sites. The drone 
will allow us to create detailed maps of the sites and give details in relation to the volumes of material 
present on these sites. 
 
Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 46 Bring Centres across the City and County.  A total of 1,862 tonnes of 
recyclables were collected from our Bring Centres for the eleven month to the end of November 2023 
compared to 1,875 tonnes for the same period in 2022. Loughboy Shopping Centre (12 tonnes collected), 
Aldi Kilkenny City (11 tonnes collected) and Newpark Shopping Centre (8.7 tonnes collected) were the 
busiest locations in the City and Aldi-Ferrybank (9.5 tonnes collected) was the busiest location outside of 
the City.  Environment staff are continuing to work very closely with our service providers to ensure the 
collection service is in keeping with demand, especially around long weekends and holiday periods. 
Dunmore Civic Amenity Site 
Our site at Dunmore continues to be one of the busiest amenity sites in the state. For the first 11 months of 
2023 we have seen an increase in the volumes of material delivered to site when compared to the same 
period in 2022.

Tidy Towns 
The final Tidy Towns forum for 2023 was held on Saturday 25th of November in Thomastown Community 
Centre.  
 
On foot of the recent National Tidy Towns results, the theme for the Forum was biodiversity. Dr Mary 
Tubridy, Ecologist and Tidy Towns adjudicator provided a presentation to members on all aspects of the

Green Schools 
The EAO continues to support 92 schools as part of the An Taisce Green Schools Programme to renew or 
attain a flag. Green schools is an international environmental education programme, offering a well defined, 
controllable way for schools to take environmental issues into the curriculum and apply them to the day-
to-day running of the school. Green schools is a holistic, long-term programme and has a two-year cycle in 
relation to preparation, assessment and attainment of a particular flag. The EAO is continuing to assist 
schools around the County to renew their membership as part of the Green Schools programme under their 
respective themes- Litter and Waste, Energy, Water, Travel, Biodiversity and Global Citizenship. Deadline 
for the applications for School Flags is March 15th, 2024.

Environment Complaints 
All Environmental complaints received are logged on the CRM (Customer Relations Management) 
System.  The number of complaints that have been received and logged by Environment staff for 
investigation so far this year up to the end of November 2023 is 868, compared with 908 for the same period 
last year (i.e. a decrease of circa 4% for the year to date).  The nature of these complaints ranges from 
littering, illegal dumping, burning of waste and abandoned cars.  Whilst every effort is made to bring 
unacceptable environmental practice into compliance, Environment Enforcement staff continue to manage 
significant enforcement cases progressing through prosecution cases. 
 
 
 
EPA Report  
The EPA ‘Focus on Local Authority Environmental Enforcement Performance Report 2022’ was published 
in November. The Report measures Local Authority performance in implementing their Recommended 
Minimum Criteria for Environmental Inspections (RMCEI) Plans for 2022. Each Local Authority RMCEI 
Plan sets out inspection targets under the National Enforcement Priorities (NEPs) across waste, air & noise, 
water and governance. In the case of Kilkenny County Council, over 2,100 inspections were contained in 
the 2022 RMCEI Plan. Unfortunately, we did not meet our targets across all NEPs in the RMCEI Plan. We 
accept the EPA Report and we take the findings seriously. We were very disappointed that we did not meet 
the high standards we set ourselves in our 2022 RMCEI Plan. The main reason for this failure was depleted 
resources during the year, with a number of long standing vacancies in the Environment section not filled.

The nature of the work involved in carrying out the majority of inspections in the RMCEI Plan is that it 
must be carried out by specialist and technical staff with the requisite skills and in some cases certification 
(e.g, to undertake septic tank inspections). 
 
It proved difficult to replace specialist staff that left the Environment Section during 2022, and this had an 
adverse knock-on impact on implementation of the RMCEI Plan. The EPA Report was not all negative and 
did acknowledge that Kilkenny County Council sets itself ambitious targets, and has strong reporting and 
complaints handling procedures in place. While the EPA Report is an important measure of performance, 
it should not be the only means of defining the work of the Environment Section. The EPA Report does not 
cover all of the work of the Environment Section. For example it does not reflect the time and resources 
involved in pursuing complex legal cases; our work with Tidy Towns that do so well each year in the 
national tidy towns awards; the fact that Kilkenny City is regularly placed in the top 10 towns in the IBAL 
League; the fact that 63% of the County is litter free and we are second only to County Kildare in this regard; 
the success of our Team Up to Clean up Event that involved almost 200 groups, resident associations and 
organisations across the County; the fact that 93% of households in relevant agglomerations have access to 
a 3-bin service; and our work in animal welfare, in particular control of dogs and horses.

Domestic Waste Water Treatment System Inspections 2023 
Under the National Inspection Plan for Domestic Wastewater Treatment Systems 2022-2026 the 
Environment Section is currently carrying out wastewater treatment inspections all over the County. All 
homeowners involved are given the statutory notice period before an inspection is carried out. From the 1st 
of January 2024, the septic tank grant will increase from €5,000 to €12,000. In order to apply for the grant all 
homeowners will either have to be inspected by the Local Authority under the National Inspection Plan or 
be located in a Prioritised Area for Action or High-Status Objective Area. 
 
Farm Inspections 
The Environment Section will carry out 80 farm inspections under our RMCEI Plan for 2023. 25 inspections 
have been carried out to date with a further 55 to be completed before end of year.  The Environment Section 
will review all inspections and issue enforcement notices if required if any breaches of the Good 
Agricultural Practice Regulations are evident on farms.  
 
Air Quality  
The Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council are making plans to install an additional air quality 
monitor in Kilkenny City. The monitor was funded by the Department Environment, Climate & 
Communications and will give additional readings for air pollutions levels in the City. 
 
The Environment Section recently held a meeting with representatives of Solid Fuel Merchants Ireland 
(SFMI) to discuss the new Solid Fuel Regulations. The Primary Focus on these regulations is on improving  
air quality and health outcomes. SFMI highlighted the issue of some unregistered fuel merchants not 
complying with current regulations and openly selling bituminous coal and turf throughout the County. 
The new Solid Fuel Regulations state it is illegal to sell or transport bituminous coal in the Republic of 
Ireland. The Environment Section are enforcing the Solid Fuel Regulations with inspections being carried 
out all over the County.  
 
Discharge License’s – Trade Effluents 
Currently the Environment Section are reviewing all 25 Discharge licenses in the County. Discharge licences 
are issued under Section 4 of the Local Government (Water Pollution) Act 1977, as amended in 1990, in 
respect of the discharge of trade effluent to surface water or groundwater. Licences set conditions so the 
discharge is treated and controlled in a manner that protects the receiving environment.

and bridge access areas took place. A working 
group was established and agreed an action plan 
based on the findings of the Walkability Study. A 
key feature of this development was the opening 
of a new walkway which links the station with the 
adjacent MacDonagh Junction Shopping Centre, 
significantly reducing the walking distance from 
the train to shops, Local Government Services and 
medical facilities.

stage process to be recognised as Age Friendly.

greatly enhanced by safety features implemented 
in this project such as good lighting, pedestrian 
crossings, set down areas, and availability of 
trained staff to help as required. The Strategic 
Oversight Committee for this Age Friendly 
project consisted of Kilkenny County Council, 
Age Friendly Ireland, Kilkenny Chamber, larnrod 
Eireann, the National Transport Authority, the 
Department of Transport, Kilkenny's Older 
Persons Council and MacDonagh Shopping 
Centre. On 21st November, 2022 Minister 
Malcolm Noonan, Minister of State for Heritage

RENT-A-ROOM SCHEME 
We have recently received a Circular from the Department regarding extending Rent-a-Room scheme 
to local authority tenancies. 
 
The broad outline of how the Scheme will to operate is as follows: 
 
▪ 
The local authority tenant advertises an available room - gov.ie/room for a student provides 
information to those wishing to rent a room to students in full time education, along with 
information for students.  
▪ 
Once the tenant and the student are happy to proceed, they apply to the local authority for consent 
for the duration of the academic year. 
▪ 
The local authority may decide to carry out a Garda check in respect of the student. 
▪ 
The local authority has discretion to approve or refuse the application. 
▪ 
Grounds for non-approval include, but are not limited to: 
 
o Rent arrears without a payment plan; 
o Overcrowding; 
o Anti-social behaviour or on good estate management grounds; 
o The property is unsuitable on other grounds e.g. size, condition, access, facilities, etc.  
 
▪ 
Following an approved application, the tenant may let the relevant room or rooms under licence 
for the duration of the student’s academic year. 
▪ 
The tenants may charge and receive a rent from the student – such rental income will be considered 
reckonable income under the local authority’s Differential Rent Scheme, with rent charged by the 
local authority according to that scheme. 
▪ 
The student will not be included on the tenant’s rent account, that is any income generated by the 
student renting a room will not be assessable for differential rent purposes.  
▪ 
All other matters, including contributions to utilities and energy costs, security deposits, disputes 
and mediation between the tenant and licensee, etc. are matters solely for the residing tenant. The 
local authority has no role in this regard. 
▪ 
Reporting of income for the purposes of availing of relevant tax relief, medical card and social 
protection disregards, when available, are matters solely for the residing tenant. 
▪ 
The local authority may request the tenant to revoke the licence on grounds of anti-social behaviour, 
overcrowding, etc. 
▪ 
The tenant is ultimately responsible for any breach of the tenancy agreement by any member of 
their household, and if necessary the local authority may issue a tenancy warning for any such 
breach. 
▪ 
At the end of the academic year, the student must vacate the property. Should the tenant and 
student wish to continue the arrangement into the next academic year, consent of the local authority 
is required.
